issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff’s tenant status supporting a claim for pre-emption was established and continued where revenue entries showed the tenancy and the competing claim did not rebut that evidence.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s tenancy was recorded in the revenue records from 1959–60 through 1968.
The purchasers claimed that the land had been leased to them in 1965, relying on a later application seeking correction of the records and a recital in the sale deed.
The sale agreement made no mention of delivery of possession, and the purchasers had not sought an entry recording their alleged tenancy before the sale.
The plaintiff pleaded that he had continuously cultivated the land as a tenant up to the institution of the suit.
There was no material showing that the relevant revenue entries were false or that the plaintiff’s tenancy had ended.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was entitled to rely on the revenue entries and was presumed to have continued as a tenant until the suit was instituted. The decrees granting pre-emption were affirmed and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 44 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act gives a rebuttable presumption of truth to the relevant revenue entries. Under Section 109 of the Indian Evidence Act, once a landlord–tenant relationship is shown, the burden of proving that it has ceased lies on the party asserting its cessation. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: tenant_based_preemption_appeal and revenue_entries_show_tenancy and entries_not_rebutted and landlord_tenant_relationship_shown and cessation_not_proved

predicates.tenant_based_preemption_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a decree granting pre-emption on the basis of the claimant’s tenancy.
predicates.revenue_entries_show_tenancy: Revenue records identify the claimant as a tenant of the land.
predicates.entries_not_rebutted: The opposing party presents no material showing that the entries recording the tenancy are false.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_shown: The evidence establishes a landlord–tenant relationship between the claimant and the person entitled to let the land.
predicates.cessation_not_proved: The party asserting that the landlord–tenant relationship ended does not prove that it ended.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns pre-emption based on tenancy, the revenue records show the claimant as tenant, those entries remain unrebutted, a landlord–tenant relationship is shown, and its cessation is not proved, the pre-emption decree is upheld.
